newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wants fast-track trade authority in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wants fast-track trade authority in 1997.

text.p: President Bill Clinton intends to seek so-called fast-track trade negotiation authority from Congress this year, White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said on Thursday.

"We are going to seek and hopefully attain it this year," McCurry said of the authority, which allows U.S. trade negotiators to reach agreements that could not be amended by Congress. Congress would have to vote to accept or reject the entire trade pact without changes.
The legislation has been delayed by a dispute between Republicans and Democrats over whether the bill should include authority to negotiate labour and environmental issues in trade deals.
Administration officials have been trying to find a compromise that would win both Democratic and Republican votes, fuelling speculation the White House might not submit a proposed bill this year.
Fast track authority is needed to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile and other trade deals.
